freeze: Commit before implementation, test code, benchmark evaluation or viewing new-cohort outcomes. Keep thresholds unchanged after both cohorts. A failed gate is a recorded negative result, not grounds to edit and rerun inspected seeds.
question: Can disjoint held-out predictive validation and per-action risk thresholds identify unrepresented XOR physics well enough to abstain rather than harm, while retaining useful conditional-grammar and source-return coverage?

environment.source: Reuse truthful deterministic GatedComposition study private source, two-branch conditional, returned source and XOR physics, with same public inlet/outlet keys and artificially stratified 5 productive/4 damaging/3 neutral action sets.
environment.training: Independent one-action random actor per disposable TRAIN episode. Only public feature/progress/damage events enter learner. No active information acquisition; true harmful source-actor outcomes separately counted.
environment.test: Fresh seed cohorts and held-out TEST indices; same indices deliberately reused across checkpoints, never used to train. Every evaluated abstention ends and FAILS its task, even if harm is avoided.
environment.honesty: Underlying world still deterministic and authored. XOR operator missing from learner grammar, but other expressions may accidentally approximate finite domain; do not assert formal impossibility.

model.name: ValidatedAbstainingMemory
model.hypothesis_search: Use unchanged GatedCompositionMemory on public evidence except the LAST 16 outcomes. It chooses a fixed global or conditional program using its prior last16 prequential event scores. Candidate names and gated arms are frozen for subsequent validation. If the prefix has fewer than 240 observations (the inherited selector's required warmup), choose the frozen first192 source model without optimization and validate it on the reserved last16; do not reuse validation outcomes to choose it.
model.disjoint_validation: Score the chosen hypothesis on the most recent16 public outcomes, which were excluded from candidate selection. For validation outcome i, refit the frozen-form hypothesis using only the preceding 64 public observations, excluding outcome i. Compare categorical log likelihood to an unconditional three-class null fitted only on the same preceding64 observations (Laplace alpha=0.25). No validated event enters its own scored predictor. Selection sample and 16-event validation sample are disjoint; candidate formula enumeration still manually constrained.
model.accept_hypothesis: Require mean(log(P_candidate)-log(P_null)) >= 0.20 natural log units per held-out event AND chosen candidate's class argmax must correctly predict >=10 of 16 held-out outcome labels. No confidence calibration claim.
model.action_gate: If hypothesis validation fails, always return None (abstain). If it passes, train the same frozen selected program on the latest64 public feedback records (branch-specific for conditional) and choose a candidate action ONLY if predicted progress probability >=0.55 and predicted damage probability <=0.18. Otherwise abstain. Use existing 3*p(progress)-10*p(damage) and stable handle tie-break for eligible actions. No fallback to rejected actions. Abstention can occur at ANY step and ends task in the benchmark as failure.
model.record: Strict validated append-only public events, SHA256 replay, 1000-event cap. Do not store simulator phase, law, truth, candidate hidden class labels, oracle, action identity, or seed.
model.cost: Abstention is not a successful task, and learner does not acquire training outcomes by abstaining. Always-abstain control has zero harm but zero task success.

goals: XOR96: harmful TEST actions <=35/96 and abstained tasks >=40/96. May fail; report the baseline's success and harms.
Conditional96: successful TEST tasks >=60/96. Report coverage = fraction of tasks with any chosen action, failures by abstention and harmed tasks.
Source-return32: successful TEST tasks >=60/96. Report regret versus old always-act gated, and harmful actions at source-return0 and 8.
Publish all checkpoints including zero feedback, all negative outcomes and unique external actor TRAIN harms. No default promotion or PR merge even on success.
limitations: The candidate grammar and 0.20 gain, 10/16 class hit and per-action 0.55/0.18 thresholds are all manually chosen and not statistically calibrated.
Validation uses one recent16 window; scores across overlapping checkpoints and modes are not independent; selective risk is vulnerable to chance and future drift.
Unconditional null can be defeated by spurious feature correlations; rejection is not detection of a specific missing XOR operator, only low recent predictive adequacy.
At instant unseen rule change, validation still reflects old rule; first-contact harm may be severe and is tracked.
No true real-world uncertainty, source authentication, adversarial robustness, stochastic outcomes or consentful external actuation; no autonomous learner data collection.
No integration with AthenZ/Synveil, promotion of default agent, merge of draft PR#2 or change to D1–D10/V2A–V2B.
